items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: The interviewee does not speak about Emil Christian; the name is only mentioned by the interviewer in the context of identifying people in a photograph.

ctx.x: That's Mr. Stevens. What's his name again? Ernie Stevens?
Yeah, Ernie Stevens, yeah, right here. And that's his two sons. They were in the service, too. And this here is Emil Christian and Tony Parenti.
She's only keeping this stuff since we moved back in this place.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: in the first bands that I've organized... Emil Christian

ctx.x: Well, I'm not sure what you played, but what you played, what you played, what you played, what you played, what you played, what you played, what you played, what you played, what you played.

Well, uh, in the first bands that I've organized, Manuel Malo, uh, Leon Malo, uh, had, uh, Frank Christian, uh, Emil Christian, and, uh, uh, uh, I can't think of his other name now. Uh, Charlie Christian. That's right. Charlie Christian. Charlie Christian. And, uh, uh, also, I had, uh, a gentleman, a fellow by the name of Ginnerman, he lived on, uh, Jackson Avenue. Well, of course, there's quite a number of these men.
